title: THE CURSOR
logline: One blinking cursor learns to code and becomes a budget line in about 5 months. But code is only 16% of developer time, and adding more cursors only multiplies the errors. A single conductor then organizes them into a software factory: Claude Opus 5.5. The clock has started again.
spine: Oct 2025: the cursor blinks at human speed. Agents 'just don't work.'
BUT on Nov 24 2025 Opus 4.5 ships, and the cursor starts writing by itself.
THEREFORE in +5 weeks, +8 weeks and +19 weeks it goes from capability to a BUDGET LINE (about 5 months).
BUT the camera pulls back. Code is one lit box in a dark line: 16% of developer time. What about the other 84%?
THEREFORE the obvious answer is more agents.
BUT flat swarms collide, and independent agents amplify errors 17.2x.
THEREFORE add structure. A coordinator brings it to 4.4x: graph for control, hierarchy for coherence, swarms for parallel work. That is THE SOFTWARE FACTORY.
BUT a factory needs someone to run the line. Who runs the line?

THEREFORE the cursor lights as conductor: Claude Opus 5.5. One session directs a dozen more, 100-agent teams pick their own structure, 18+ hours unattended, Fable 5.1-level work at 40% lower cost than Opus 5.
BUT the clock has restarted. If the pattern holds, budgets arrive in early 2027 (labeled as a projection). One cursor, now staying ON.
motifs: CURSOR ▮ (the protagonist): a lone ice-blue cursor blinking on the tick (human speed) -> a clay spark that types by itself (Opus 4.5) -> a city of cursors and a rising column (wave one) -> cursors piled against dark walls, then a red flat swarm (the problem) -> the conductor cursor wiring 12 sub-leads (coordination) -> a monolith at the head of the line -> a factory built of cursor blocks -> one cursor alone again that stops blinking and stays ON (button). Match cuts on its rectangle: cursor -> gate -> wall -> monolith -> title slot.
THE LIGHT LINE: the cursor's code trail -> the BUDGET LINE ledger slot -> the delivery line -> clay threads from the conductor to every station -> the title's light-line forge.

GATES / WALLS: month gates the camera flies through at accelerating intervals (progress, L->R) -> dark station walls the cursors pile against (REVIEW, TEST, DEPLOY, ON-CALL) -> glass gates the work flows through, ice in and clay out (the mirror callback in Act 3).

THE TICK (light and sound): the cursor blink is phase-locked to the tick at 120 BPM. It breaks to double time when Opus 4.5 ships, is the only sound at the midpoint and the drop, lifts to 150 BPM in Act 3 and returns alone in the button.

why_it_works:
The whole argument rides on one shape the viewer never loses: the cursor. It starts as an ice-blue blink at human speed. It turns clay and writes by itself, multiplies into a city, piles up against dark walls, floods in as a red swarm, rises as a coordinator, stands as a monolith at the head of the line and finally sits alone and stays ON. Match cuts on its rectangle carry each change. That gives an executive audience a protagonist and a place instead of a slideshow.

The story is a strict BUT/THEREFORE chain built only from facts.md:
- Karpathy's doubt.
- Opus 4.5.
- The +5, +8 and +19 week gates.
- About 5 months to budget.
- The 16% reversal.
- 'More agents' failing at 17.2x.
- A coordinator bringing it to 4.4x.
- The factory.
- 'Who runs the line?'
- Four literal proof beats, each paired with a matching image (12 threads, 40 green PRs, 100 orbs splitting into 12 clusters, 6 lanes).

The proof cards carry their source tags. Vendor claims are labeled as such, and the projection is labeled PROJECTION.

The client's "top angle, bottom angle" request has a meaning attached:
- Worm's-eye shows threat and awe.
- Top-down shows understanding: the single 4 s midpoint pull-back is the moment the viewer sees the dark line.
- FPV shows speed.
- Symmetric low hero shots show order after the camera rights itself at 72.0.

Pacing follows a sawtooth: Act 1 ASL 1.7 s, Act 2A 0.96 s, Act 2C 0.83 s, Act 3 0.91 s on a faster 150 BPM grid. The 8 s tick-only midpoint dip and three short silences make the three braams land. The peak sits at 87% of runtime, followed by a false stop, a 4.8 s title and a button that restarts the clock and ends on the same single cursor the film began with.

Text is held to 135 words across the film. Every card is staged as a world object (gate numerals, a ledger stamp, floor signage) or a slam on a hit. Every shot uses only engine primitives: glowBoxes, particles, fatLines, beams, textPlanes and the grid.
risks: 'THE OTHER 84%?' is arithmetic from Atlassian's 16%. Shot 49 maps the remaining 84% onto REVIEW/TEST/DEPLOY/ON-CALL stations, but Atlassian's remainder also includes meetings and other non-delivery time. Keep the stations as illustration and add no claim card that equates them.

GRAPH·CONTROL / HIERARCHY·COHERENCE / SWARM·PARALLEL come from the brief's design framing. They are supported by the Google coordinator finding and the 'one writer per change' rule of thumb, but they are not a measured result. Present them as labels only, never as 'proven'.

The BUDGET LINE ledger, the desk city and the agent counts in the non-proof shots are visualizations. Only the proof shots use literal counts (12, 40, 100, 6 lanes). Do not imply that a single Opus 5.5 team numbered in the thousands.

Opus 5.5 is not Anthropic's most capable model. Use no superlatives and no Terminal-Bench 'top' card. The Fable card must keep 'VS OPUS 5' and the ANTHROPIC tag (vendor claim). The run-rate card must keep ANTHROPIC-REPORTED.

Quotes are shortened with ellipses ('…never felt this much behind…'), and Karpathy's 'they just don't work' referred to agents as interns or employees. Keep the attribution tags visible for at least 0.8 s.

The 150 BPM lift at 92.0 s (frame 2760): engine beats() is global, so Act 3 shots need a per-section beat helper (0.4 s) or literal seconds, and the audio cue list must switch grids on the exact frame.
Engine music sections are reused under different names: the 'act3' bed plays the full-hybrid Act 2C (1:04–1:28), and 'peak' plays Act 3. Confirm the composer and renderer use this mapping.

Render budget: about 133 s at roughly 0.7 s per 3D frame is about 1.5 h. Fields above 2,000 instanced meshes (the desk city, the cursor fields, the 20k swarm) must be particles, staying at or under 30k per shot. Black and type-only shots (81, 82, 110–113, 116) are cheap.

Photosensitivity: the flutter and recall shots (79, 109) cut at 3–8f and must be luminance-matched within ±8% with no full-field white. There are 7 flashes in total, never more than 3 in any 1 s window, and no saturated red full-field flash during the error contagion.
Read time: the 6-word proof cards get 2.4 s each, which is tight on phones. Keep cap height at 7% or more, camera motion at 3°/s or less while text is up, and background at -0.8 stop under the text.
The word count is 135 of 140, so there is no title tagline. If the client wants one, cut the end-card credit lines (10 words).
'THAT WAS WAVE ONE.' and 'who runs the line?' are narrative framing, not claims. The '+5/+8/+19 WEEKS' gates are measured from Nov 24 2025, as in facts.md.
